description: Run list for the Past Analyses UI page, newest first, with per-run candidate counts joined in.
signature: def list_runs(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, limit: int = 50, offset: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame
docstring:
List runs newest-first with pagination.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    limit: Maximum rows to return.
    offset: Rows to skip, for pagination.

Returns:
    A DataFrame with columns: run_id, started_at, finished_at, status, trigger_type, candidate_count (count of games_enriched rows for that run_id, 0 if enrichment has not run yet), sorted by started_at descending.
postconditions: Result is sorted strictly by started_at descending, ties broken by run_id descending (consistent with run_id being timestamp-prefixed)
candidate_count is always a non-negative integer, never NaN, even for a run with no games_enriched rows yet

edge_cases.input: No runs exist in the database
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns an empty DataFrame with the correct column set (not a DataFrame with zero columns)

edge_cases.input: offset beyond the total row count
edge_cases.expected_behavior: returns an empty DataFrame, not an error

edge_cases.input: A run with status='pending' and zero games_enriched rows

unit_tests.name: test_list_runs_newest_first
unit_tests.description: Three runs created in sequence are returned in reverse creation order.

unit_tests.name: test_list_runs_empty_database
unit_tests.description: No runs -> empty DataFrame with expected columns.

unit_tests.name: test_list_runs_pagination
unit_tests.description: limit=1, offset=1 returns exactly the second-newest run.
unit_tests.expected: single-row DataFrame for the second-newest run
